newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up on widespread buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up on widespread buying.

text.p: Colombo share prices closed higher on Thursday on widespread retail and local institutional buying, brokers said.
They said a combination of positive factors like rains in the last few days and improved political sentiment led to active trading in blue chips and second line stocks.
The Colombo all share index ended 4.52 points higher at 652.9 on a turnover of 94 million rupees.
"Power was a major concern, but with rains coming the market seems to be settled for a bull run," said Shafi Waheed of CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch stock brokers.
Last year's power cuts due to a drought hurt corporate profits.

"Everybody was buying. There are a combination of factors -- rains, liquidity in the market and political stability. We expect the market to move higher with emphasis on weaker shares, said Sarinda Unamboowe of brokers John Keells.
A recent agreement between Sri Lanka's two main political parties to work together to end the country's ethnic war has buoyed market sentiment.
Shares of Commercial Bank ended 5.25 rupees up at 170.25, CTC Eagle 1.50 rupees at 50.50, Ceylon Breweries 2.25 rupees up at 50.25 and John Keells Holdings up five rupees at 210.
